meta.title: Isolate pull-request validation from trusted release infrastructure
meta.author: Codex manager

feature.problem_statement: Pull-request validation currently executes repository-controlled code on the same configurable self-hosted runner family used for release publication, with Docker and sudo-capable operations that can persist or reach trusted infrastructure.
goals: Run untrusted pull-request validation on an ephemeral, non-release runner class with read-only permissions and no persisted checkout credentials.
Make release publication use a distinct trusted runner class and protected-main-only trigger with narrowly scoped permissions.
Add fail-closed workflow contract checks and operator documentation that distinguish repository controls from external runner, network, and teardown evidence.
Preserve the existing validate status-check contract while making trust-boundary violations visible before merge.
non_goals: Provisioning or changing Codicarium runner pools, autoscaling, VM wipe, Docker isolation, firewall egress, or GitHub organization policy from this repository PR.
Publishing secrets, tokens, credentials, or raw runner telemetry.
Replacing the existing comprehensive make ci validation with an untested partial suite.
scope_in: .github/workflows/ci.yml PR runner, permissions, checkout credential, and trust-contract changes
.github/workflows/release.yml trusted runner selector, protected-main trigger/guard, permissions, and checkout credential changes
Static workflow trust checker/tests and Makefile integration
scope_out: External runner infrastructure and live fork/teardown canaries
Supply-chain action SHA pinning tracked by issue #124
Changing application or Helm runtime behavior

requirements.statement: PR validation must resolve to an ephemeral GitHub-hosted runner or an explicitly dedicated single-use PR pool and must never fall back to the shared release self-hosted label.
requirements.rationale: Repository-controlled PR code is untrusted and must not share mutable release capacity.

requirements.statement: PR validation must have read-only job permissions, no repository secrets, and checkout must not persist credentials.
requirements.rationale: A validation job must not expose write authority or reusable credentials to arbitrary PR code.

requirements.statement: Release publication must run only from protected main pushes on a distinct trusted release runner selector with publication permissions scoped to the release job.
requirements.rationale: Publication credentials and deployment automation must never be available to arbitrary branch execution.

requirements.statement: A fail-closed static workflow contract checker and focused tests must reject shared PR/release runner selectors, unsafe PR triggers or permissions, persisted checkout credentials, and unrestricted release refs.
requirements.rationale: The trust boundary must be reviewable and regression-tested in the repository.

requirements.statement: Operator documentation must describe fork, agent-generated, human-authored, protected-main, PR-runner, and release-runner trust classes plus the external evidence required for teardown, network, Docker, cache, and cleanup attestation.
requirements.rationale: Static workflow changes cannot prove platform isolation; operators need an explicit evidence contract.

requirements.statement: The implementation must retain the existing validate check and comprehensive validation coverage, and must not claim issue completion until external runner and cleanup evidence is verified.
requirements.rationale: The merge gate and honest completion state are required for safe rollout.

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Given the repository workflows, when the workflow contract checker evaluates the PR job, then it fails for self-hosted/Linux/codicarium or release labels and passes only for the approved ephemeral PR runner policy.
Given the CI workflow, when the checker evaluates permissions, secrets, and checkout, then it proves read-only permissions, no secrets, and persist-credentials=false.

Given the release workflow, when the checker evaluates triggers, runner selection, and permissions, then it proves push-only protected-main execution on the distinct trusted selector with publication permissions absent from PR jobs.

Given the operator runbook and issue evidence, when an operator reviews the trust model, then repository-verifiable controls are separated from platform-admin fork, runner-destruction, egress, Docker, and cleanup-attestation evidence.

Given the candidate commit, when focused tests, actionlint, workflow parsing, full repository CI, and hosted validation run, then all pass and the issue remains open/blocked if external evidence is absent.

test_plan.approach: Run focused Python workflow-contract tests with fixtures for safe and unsafe runner, trigger, permission, checkout, and release-ref configurations.
Run make workflow-parse, actionlint, YAML parsing, and the Makefile trust-check target against the repository workflows.
Inspect hosted PR/release job metadata and platform runner inventory; require distinct labels/groups and teardown/egress evidence, treating missing evidence as a blocker.
Run make ci and verify exact-head GitHub validate success with no test-owned containers, networks, or generated tracked changes left behind.
Platform-admin fork canary and disposable-runner cleanup attestation review before issue closure.

review_checks: No shared self-hosted label or mutable fallback in PR path
validation_checks: Hosted PR runner metadata and platform teardown evidence

review_checks: Read-only permissions; no secrets; checkout credentials disabled
validation_checks: Actionlint and exact hosted job permissions

review_checks: Push-only protected main and distinct trusted selector
validation_checks: Hosted release metadata and protected-main evidence

review_checks: Fail-closed contract tests cover unsafe mutations
Documentation does not overclaim external isolation
validation_checks: Docs checker and platform evidence checklist

review_checks: validate contract retained; issue closure gated on evidence
validation_checks: make ci; exact-head hosted validate; clean resources

perspectives.summary: Use GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 for PR validation, a distinct codicarium-release pool for publication, read-only PR permissions, persist-credentials=false, and document external runner/firewall/attestation prerequisites.

Current CI and release share self-hosted Linux/codicarium capacity; repository changes can separate labels and permissions, but runner ephemerality, Docker isolation, egress policy, and teardown attestations require platform evidence.

Untrusted PR code has shell, Docker, sudo, cache, and network execution on mutable runners; fail closed against shared labels, unsafe triggers, secrets/write permissions, persisted checkout credentials, and arbitrary release refs.

Static contracts, actionlint, workflow parsing, and hosted metadata can verify repository policy; fork canaries, runner destruction, network isolation, and cleanup attestation require platform-admin evidence.

council.consensus_summary: Implement repository-enforceable trust-boundary hardening and fail-closed workflow contract tests now; track dedicated runner pools, egress/Docker isolation, and cleanup attestation as explicit external validation prerequisites.
open_questions: Can platform provision and attest dedicated PR and release runner pools before the PR is merged?
Which exact Codicarium runner labels/groups and release environment reviewers will be available?
Can a fork canary be run for this private repository or an approved test repository?
